questions.text: How does Habakkuk begin his complaint (Habakkuk 1:2)?

options.text: O LORD, why hast thou forsaken me, and wherefore hidest thou thyself?
O LORD, how long shall I cry, and thou wilt not hear unto my prayer?
O LORD, wherefore doth thine anger burn, and why dost thou not save us?
O LORD, send now a deliverer to break the heavy yoke of the heathen!

questions.text: Whom does the LORD raise up according to Habakkuk 1:6?

options.text: The Assyrians, a cruel and warlike nation
The Egyptians, a strong and mighty nation
The Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation
The Persians, a fierce and renowned nation

questions.text: What question does Habakkuk ask in Habakkuk 1:13?

options.text: Wherefore hast thou called me, and wherefore dost thou hide thy face from us?
Wherefore dost thou smite thy chosen people, and why dost thou not deliver us?
Wherefore dost thou suffer the heathen to come, and wilt not defend thy land?
Wherefore lookest thou upon them that deal treacherously, and holdest thy tongue?

questions.text: How does Habakkuk await the answer of the LORD according to Habakkuk 2:1?

options.text: He stands upon his watch and sets him upon the tower to see what will be said unto him
He departs into the solitary wilderness and there prays for an answer of the LORD
He goes into the holy temple and there waits patiently until God shall answer him
He asks the priests and elders and waits quietly to hear what they shall tell him

questions.text: What principle is stated in Habakkuk 2:4?

options.text: The just shall prevail by his strength
The just shall live by his faith
The just shall rest in quiet peace
The just shall reap what he sowed

questions.text: With what words does Habakkuk 2 conclude the woes (Habakkuk 2:20)?

options.text: The LORD judgeth all idols; let all the earth keep silence before him
The LORD is King on mount Zion; let all the earth keep silence before him
The LORD is in his holy temple; let all the earth keep silence before him
The LORD hath created all things; let all the earth keep silence before him

questions.text: What does Habakkuk plead in Habakkuk 3:2?

options.text: O LORD, send us rain in the land; when famine cometh, remember us in mercy
O LORD, destroy the enemy in the midst of the years; when trouble is near, judge
O LORD, grant us a righteous king; when contention ariseth, establish peace
O LORD, revive thy work in the midst of the years; in wrath remember mercy

questions.text: How does Habakkuk 3:3 describe the coming of God?

options.text: God came from Teman and the Holy One from mount Paran; his glory covered the heavens
God came in a thick cloud from Sinai; the whole earth trembled before his great glory
God came from mount Zion and the hills of Seir; the whole earth was moved at his word
God came from the sea in brightness of fire; the heavens were filled with his splendour

questions.text: With what confession does Habakkuk conclude (Habakkuk 3:17-18)?

options.text: Although I suffer affliction, yet will I wait in silence for salvation
Although the fig tree shall not blossom, yet I will rejoice in the LORD
Although the enemy cometh upon us, yet will I trust in the arm of flesh
Although destruction be at hand, yet will I look unto the earthly gates

questions.text: To what are the horses of the Chaldeans compared in Habakkuk 1:8?

options.text: Swifter than the leopards and more fierce than the evening wolves
Swifter than the harts and more fierce than the foxes of the morning
Swifter than the eagles and more fierce than the lions of the desert
Swifter than the arrows and more fierce than the hunters of the forest

questions.text: Unto what do the Chaldeans sacrifice according to Habakkuk 1:16?

options.text: Unto their swift horses and unto their chariots
Unto their mighty kings and unto their princes
Unto their net and burn incense unto their drag
Unto their sharp sword and unto their bent bow

questions.text: What was Habakkuk commanded to do with the vision in Habakkuk 2:2?

options.text: Proclaim it unto the king that he may warn the people in time
Seal it up and hide it in the sanctuary until the end of time
Recite it aloud in the temple until the people turn to the LORD
Write the vision and make it plain upon tables, that he may run

questions.text: What is said of the vision in Habakkuk 2:3, though it tarry?

options.text: Wait for it, because it will surely come, it will not tarry
Doubt of it, because it is reserved only for the wise elders
Cry it aloud, because it shall be fulfilled only by fasting
Forget it, because it shall not come to pass for many years

questions.text: With what shall the earth be filled according to Habakkuk 2:14?

options.text: With the righteousness of the faithful, as the dew covereth the field
With the knowledge of the glory of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea
With the fear of the Almighty, as the thick clouds cover all the heavens
With the sacrifices of the nations, as the smoke covereth the mountains

questions.text: What is said in Habakkuk 2:19 of him that saith to the wood, Awake?

options.text: Blessed is he, for that which is laid over with gold heareth his cry
Woe unto him, for the wood shall awake and punish him for his wickedness
Woe unto him, for it is laid over with gold and there is no breath in it
Blessed is he, for that which is laid over with gold showeth God's presence

questions.text: Like what will the LORD make the prophet's feet according to Habakkuk 3:19?

options.text: Like lions' paws to protect him along his dangerous way
Like horses' hoofs to carry him through the dark valley
Like eagles' wings to bear him swiftly over all his foes
Like hinds' feet to make him walk upon his high places

questions.text: Which two shortages does Habakkuk 3:17 name, despite which he will joy in the LORD?

options.text: There shall be no herd in the stalls
There shall be no water in the wells
There shall be no shepherd with the flock
Neither shall fruit be in the vines

questions.text: Whose dwellings did Habakkuk see in affliction according to Habakkuk 3:7?

options.text: The tents of Cushan and the curtains of the land of Midian
The tents of Ammon and the curtains of the land of the Hittites
The tents of the Philistines and the curtains of the Amalekites
The tents of Moab and the curtains of the land of the Edomites
